correctness.rationale: For smooth origin-containing convex bodies, normal-speed-one first variation splits into a nonnegative mean-curvature term and the radial Laplacian volume integral. Ball inclusion bounds these by respectively n(n−1)ω_n S^{n−2}φ(S) and nω_n S^{n−1}φ′(S), exactly G′(S). Integration proves the sharp parallel increment, retaining the omitted positive Laplacian volume yields the deficit bound. Convex regularization plus published continuity extends to degenerate bodies. Origin-anchored monotonicity and N-step Minkowski interpolation yield the global exact G′(R) Hausdorff constant, which concentric balls approach. The point flux condition validates divergence at the origin; positivity establishes strictness for power weights. Finite checker is auxiliary, not a substitute for the proof.

value.rationale: The exact Hausdorff sensitivity of a natural weighted boundary energy is needed in radius-constrained convex shape optimization, extending qualitative continuity to an optimal all-dimensional quantitative theorem. Unlike a routine continuity bound, it identifies the extremal ball, gives a strict Laplacian-weighted geometric deficit for every outer parallel body, and closes the precise constant gap left for 0<p<1 by the closest planar work. Singular gradients at the origin, lower-dimensional degeneration and all-dimensional convexity are handled without smoothness of the unknown body.
